In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the paper presents a learning theory based framework for cache update and performance evaluation for the caching problem with unknown and non-stationary popularity profiles, and provides a high probability bound for the offloading loss.
the proposed cache update algorithm is the first to provide an offloading loss bound with a finite sample size and a finite number of time slots for non-stationary popularity profiles.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel caching cost function and study it from a novel perspective of learning theory.

the proposed algorithm is robust against non-stationary popularity profiles, and the offloading loss is minimized by learning the popularity profile online, and adapting the cache content periodically.
the offloading loss can be bounded with high probability by a function that depends on the Rademacher and mixing coefficients and the number of time-slots.
The main takeaway from our work is that
caching with time-varying popularity profiles can be performed efficiently, and it is not necessary to update the cache contents periodically, which can be very costly in practice.
caching is more effective when the popularity profile is stationary, which can be verified by our simulation results.
